openDecisions.question: Which Characters are 'visible' for charactersCount, taggedCharactersCount and totalCharactersCount?
options: a) deleted_at IS NULL AND archived_at IS NULL (global list defaults), hidden-profile characters included
b) a) plus hide_profile_as_spoiler = false (exact default of GET /api/characters)
openDecisions.codebaseFacts: Global list defaults archived=false and includeHiddenProfiles=false (global-character-filter.ts:17,27; characters.repository.ts:1025-1031). hideProfileAsSpoiler is a spoiler mask toggled by PATCH /api/characters/:id (characters.ts UpdateCharacterSchema). archivedAt is only written by portability import.
openDecisions.recommendation: a). Archive and trash are lifecycle states; the spoiler mask is presentation. Under b) a spoiler toggle would move tag counts and force use-update-character to invalidate Tag aggregates.
openDecisions.answer: a — spoiler-hidden Characters count if not deleted/archived; the spoiler flag only masks the profile

openDecisions.question: How to satisfy the Tag.type invariant when dev/prod data cannot be inspected from here
options: a) open the dev tunnel (:5532), SELECT type counts read-only, add a migration only if a bad row exists
b) ship an idempotent data migration UPDATE ... SET type='custom' WHERE type NOT IN (6 values) regardless; no-op on clean DBs
c) b) plus a raw-SQL CHECK constraint on tags.type
openDecisions.codebaseFacts: Column is TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'custom' (20260716184304_enrich_tags), so null is impossible. Every code writer is canonical (CreateTagSchema/UpdateTagSchema via TagTypeSchema; upsertByNormalized uses the default). Local booknest_dev has 0 tags; dev port 5532 refused.
openDecisions.recommendation: b). Cheap, env-independent, and proves the invariant at deploy time in every environment. c) adds a raw-SQL object Prisma cannot see, for a risk no code path produces.
openDecisions.answer: b — idempotent data migration: non-canonical type -> custom

openDecisions.question: Should POST/PATCH reject colors outside the 8-color palette?
options: a) tighten shared color schema to the palette enum
b) keep the permissive hex/token schema; only read models resolve to parchment
openDecisions.codebaseFacts: TagColorSchema accepts any hex or token up to 32 chars (tags.ts:40-49). The only FE writer sends palette values. Existing API tests post '#A96E47'.
openDecisions.recommendation: a). 02 §13 lists 'canonical palette color' under validation, and it stops new non-palette rows from appearing. Cost: five superseded test fixtures.
openDecisions.answer: a — POST/PATCH accept only the 8 canonical colors; legacy read as parchment

openDecisions.question: Literal 'type[]' / 'color[]' parameter names, or the repo's multi-value convention?
options: a) names 'type' and 'color', nuqs parseAsArrayOf (comma) in URL, queryStringArray on the API (repeated or comma)
b) literal bracket names 'type[]' and 'color[]' in URL and API
openDecisions.codebaseFacts: Genres uses 'group' with parseAsArrayOf (genres-query.ts:90) and queryStringArray (genres.ts:81). No bracket-named params exist in the repo.
openDecisions.recommendation: a). Treat '[]' in the spec as notation for multi-value; b) needs custom nuqs keys and Orval param names for no user benefit.
openDecisions.answer: a — same as Genres: parseAsArrayOf comma format ?type=trope,theme (user confirmed 2026-09-23 after correction)

openDecisions.question: nuqs history mode for committed Tags state
options: a) history: 'push' for committed q/filter/type/color/sort changes
openDecisions.codebaseFacts: Genres uses default replace; notes uses push for one transition (use-notes-archive-query.ts:58). F-URL-03 requires back/forward to restore state.
openDecisions.recommendation: a). With replace, Back leaves /tags instead of restoring the previous filter, which fails F-URL-03.
openDecisions.answer: a — history push for committed q/filter/type/color/sort

openDecisions.question: Remove GET /api/tags/stats and TagStatsView after the new page ships?
options: a) remove in Phase 6 and move the trash-isolation assertion to /api/tags/catalog
openDecisions.codebaseFacts: Only consumer is features/tags/api/use-tag-stats.ts; tests at tags.controller.test.ts:258-330, tags.service.test.ts:258, book-trash-isolation.controller.test.ts:149.
openDecisions.recommendation: a). After T61 it has zero runtime consumers and duplicates the catalog with Book-only usage, which 02 §19 rejects.
openDecisions.answer: a — delete GET /api/tags/stats in cleanup once no consumers

openDecisions.question: Where catalog filtering/sorting/pagination runs
options: a) in SQL: one aggregate CTE, WHERE/ORDER BY/LIMIT in Postgres
b) Genres pattern: load one aggregate row per tag, filter/sort/page in a pure domain module
openDecisions.codebaseFacts: Genres does b) (genre-list.ts) over a bounded system catalog. tags.name already has uk-UA-x-icu collation, so SQL name ordering matches the Ukrainian collator.
openDecisions.recommendation: a) for catalog and facets, since 02 §17 says not to load every tag into memory to filter/count. Summary can assemble in a pure domain function from one GROUP BY result for testability.
openDecisions.answer: a — catalog/filter/sort/pagination/facets in SQL; summary one centralized implementation with the same usage semantics

openDecisions.question: The spec's final verification lists 'pnpm test' and 'pnpm build'; CLAUDE.md §9 makes the local full suite opt-in
options: a) run pnpm test locally once at the end
b) push the branch and use the green CI run as evidence
openDecisions.codebaseFacts: Full suite takes about 7 minutes and saturates the machine (CLAUDE.md §9).
openDecisions.recommendation: b), plus targeted vitest locally per slice. Pick a) if you want local proof before pushing.
openDecisions.answer: b — local typecheck, lint, targeted tests, /blast-radius; full suite in CI after push, push only with explicit consent
